candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential; identify risk factors for complications and increase surveillance/preparedness when risk is elevated
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — recognition of uterine-atony risk factors
candidate.educational_objective: Identify prolonged labor and uterine overdistention from multifetal gestation or polyhydramnios as factors that increase the risk for postpartum uterine atony and hemorrhage.

options.A: A client with prolonged labor and marked uterine overdistention from a multifetal pregnancy with polyhydramnios
options.B: A client with an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy and normally progressing labor without uterine overdistention
options.C: A client whose only finding is a healed remote ankle sprain and no obstetric complications
options.D: A client with normal uterine size and no intrapartum risk factors who asks about routine postpartum care

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Uterine atony occurs when the postpartum myometrium does not contract effectively enough to compress placental-bed vessels. Authoritative NCBI/StatPearls guidance identifies prolonged labor and uterine distention—including multifetal gestation and polyhydramnios—as recognized risk factors. A client with several of these factors warrants heightened hemorrhage preparedness and postpartum uterine assessment. B and D lack the stated risk factors, and C is unrelated to uterine contractility.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Prolonged labor and uterine overdistention from multiple gestation or polyhydramnios increase the risk of uterine atony, a major cause of postpartum hemorrhage.
